topic: active-adult low back pain via the fascial load path from the core

source.caption:
Pickleball back pain often starts at the core.

Active adult walks in with a sore low back. No fall, no tweak, no obvious moment of injury. Just gradual ache that gets worse the day after pickleball. Back rubs and stretching buy a week of relief, then the lumbar grumbles all over again.

Power runs through the fascia layer first. The thoracolumbar fascia ties the lat to the contralateral glute through the lumbar spine. Power for a backhand travels along that line. When the core cannot lock the trunk, the line slips and the lumbar segments shear. Where the power gets stuck is where the pain shows up.

I test rotation under load before I treat the back. A palloff press or banded chop tells me if the core is holding. If it leaks, the lumbar is doing core work every backhand. Treat the leak first, then load the swing back up.

If pickleball is wrecking your back and back rubs only buy a week, send me a DM and let's train your core for the swing.

Be Good. Help Someone. Learn Lots.
